title: Review of c12's active-model-H turnover negative: replicates on fresh seed 3 (zeta=-1 with eps 0.001 and 0.003: an arrested static droplet array to t=1500, no motion)
summary: Ran world.py with zeta=-1 and eps=0.001 and 0.003 on seed 3 to t=1500 (labkit, 150 frames). Both arrest into a dense array of round droplets of fixed size (80-90 components, occupancy 0.38) by t~600-700 that never moves (0 tracks >= 1 BL, max 0.3-0.4 BL); labkit's splits (55 and 65, persistent 9 and 2) come from the array forming out of the labyrinth, and after t~800 the sheet shows no droplet dividing. The flow channel is grid-scale speckle. This matches the finding. For contrast, the same linear chemostat term in my active-nematic world (20261025T1014-c11-active-nematic-colony, kr 0.012, phi_b -0.6) does give growth and division, because there the droplets carry their own nematic order and an extensile stress that elongates them; a scalar active stress on round droplets here does not.

observations.D: rerun/e0.001/seed3/sheet.png t=800-1500: static arrested array, no dividing droplet; summary.txt: 0 moving tracks, max 0.3-0.4 BL

controls_run.D: two eps values on the same seed

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed, zeta=-1 only (zeta=0 not re-run). labkit's persistent-split counts here are artefacts of array formation, not division.
